item.text:
## Creating the invitation

On the members settings page, [settings/members/page.tsx](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/members/page.tsx) loads the organization’s `Actor`, checks `member:invite` to decide whether to show the form, and passes the current seat check to [invite-member-form.tsx](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/components/domain/member/invite-member-form.tsx). The form checks `inviteMemberSchema` before submission. That schema requires a valid email of at most 254 characters and lowercases it; the role defaults to `member`. The `invitableRoleSchema` allows `admin`, `member`, or `viewer`, but not `owner`. `RoleSelect` also filters options by the inviter’s role.

The server action [invite-member.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/actions/members/invite-member.ts) runs through `withAction`, which validates the input again and resolves the session to an active organization member. Then it checks `can(actor, "member:invite", ...)`; the permission matrix in [permissions.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/lib/permissions.ts) requires admin or owner. The action consumes the organization’s `member:invite` rate limit, loads an organization summary, and rejects if the usage counter plus one would exceed the plan’s seat limit.

Next, `invitation-service.ts` runs `inviteMember` and `inviteMembers`. They recheck tenant scope and invite permission, consume the same rate-limit bucket again, require the organization to exist, and count active members plus pending invitations against the plan’s seat limit. The active-member count comes from live membership rows; pending invitations are rows with neither `acceptedAt` nor `revokedAt`. That pending count does not exclude expired invitations. There is no check that the address is already a member or already has an invitation. The schema accepts an optional `message`, but the service neither stores nor uses it.

## What is stored, and what reaches the email

After those checks, `inviteMembers` generates a random 32-byte URL-safe token and gives its SHA-256 hash to `insertInvitation`. The [invitations table](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/server/db/schema/members.ts) stores the organization, email, role, inviter, token hash, expiry, accepted/revoked timestamps, and normal IDs and timestamps. The expiry is set to 14 days by `DEFAULT_EXPIRY_DAYS` in `invitation-service.ts`.

There is a gap in the described flow: **the current invite path does not send an email or build an accept URL.** The raw token is local to `inviteMembers` and is discarded after the hash is stored. Although [invite-email.tsx](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/emails/invite-email.tsx) has an `acceptUrl` button and [emails/render.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/emails/render.ts) can render it, `inviteMembers` calls neither. Also, [\_mappers.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/server/repositories/_mappers.ts) maps the stored hash into the returned `Invitation.token` field, which the action returns to the client. That value is the hash, not the raw link credential; putting it in `/invite/[token]` would fail because acceptance hashes the submitted token again. And [email-service.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/server/services/email-service.ts) only writes email metadata to a log when called; it has no outbound mail transport.

After inserting the invitation, the service emits `member.invited`. The activity listener records an “Invited … as …” entry. The action then revalidates member and invitation views. Neither step supplies the missing raw token to an email.

## Using an invitation link

If a valid raw token is supplied to [invite/[token]/page.tsx](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/app/(auth)/invite/[token]/page.tsx), the page checks only its format at first. A signed-out visitor is sent to login with the invite route as the destination. The page does not look up the invitation; the user must be signed in before the accept form is shown.

On submit, [invite-accept-form.tsx](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/app/(auth)/invite/[token]/invite-accept-form.tsx) passes the token to `acceptInvitationAction` in [accept-invitation.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/actions/members/accept-invitation.ts). The action validates the token again and requires a live session. `invitation-service.acceptInvitation` hashes the raw token, looks up that hash, and rejects a missing, revoked, already accepted, or expired invitation.

Acceptance does **not** compare the signed-in account’s email with the invitation’s stored email. The token is the credential, so anyone signed in with a valid session who obtains it can accept it. If that user already has a live membership row, the service returns it early without marking this invitation accepted. Otherwise it inserts an active member row with the invitation’s role and inviter and a `joinedAt` timestamp, marks the invitation accepted, and emits `member.joined`.

There is a seat check in `acceptInvitationAction`, but it runs **after** those writes and the event. It resolves the new member as an `Actor`, loads the organization summary, and rejects if the usage counter is now over the plan limit. If that check fails, the membership and accepted invitation have already been written; there is no rollback. On success, the form redirects to the `org` query parameter if present, otherwise to `/orgs`.

## What changes for the rest of the app

`member.joined` is wired through [instrumentation.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/instrumentation.ts) and [event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/server/services/event-registry.ts). The usage listener in [usage-service.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/server/services/usage-service.ts) increments `seatsUsed`; the notification listener in [notification-service.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/server/services/notification-service.ts) creates a notification for the organization owner, subject to notification preferences. The activity service records `member.invited`, but has no `member.joined` listener, and the webhook service has no member-join listener.

The membership row is what grants ongoing access: `resolveActor` and `resolveActorForOrg` in [member-service.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/server/services/member-service.ts) and [session-service.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/c24d2041-29c8-4298-a5ef-5b55a59d3055/src/server/services/session-service.ts) read its active status and role to construct the `Actor` used by permission checks. The member list and seat counts also read the membership table, so subsequent requests can treat the colleague as a workspace member.
